attributes.bisect_verdict: DC'S CAP WAS UNBISECTED AND ITS FRAMING WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Edit A (the TextLinesWidth inline helper) ALONE measured real 172 / fuzzy 72.0744% - WORSE than DC's combined state (real 168 / fuzzy 71.91% on real, better on fuzzy) and worse than baseline on both, so a metric-only bisect would have re-reverted it. But Edit A alone closed the frame to 248 = target EXACTLY and took the slot map from 0-of-6 matching to 5-of-8, which is what made the true residual readable. Edit B (merging buf1[18] and buf2[20] into one buffer) is REFUTED OUTRIGHT by the target's own slot geometry: target's array bases are +36 and +108 with the save area at +188, so the two arrays are 72 and 80 bytes and are DISTINCT - and the 72-byte (18-element) one is declared LAST, which a single merged buffer cannot reproduce. DC's fakematch note that 'the original plainly reused ONE scratch array' is therefore wrong; the two-array split is the faithful form, and only their DECLARATION ORDER needed swapping. THE REAL BLOCKER WAS NEVER THE FRAME. It was three source-shape defects the frame work masked, all read directly off the target CFG: (1) ARM ORDER AND EARLY RETURN - target branches `blt` at 0x48 to the loop arm at 0x104 and falls through to the SINGLE-index arm at 0x60, then emits `li r3,0; b <epilogue>` for the out-of-range case, i.e. the source tested `idx >= 0` first and used `if (idx >= e->count) return 0;` (the idiom its already-matching sibling StringTextHeightSub uses), NOT an `else { maxw = 0; }` merge; this single change moved real 180 -> 116 and fuzzy 72.15 -> 87.81; (2) OPCODE-FORM TRIPLE - `cmplw` vs target `cmpw` (comparison operands are signed, so `prev`/`color` are s32 not u32), `bge` vs target `ble` (the source wrote `if (w > max)`, not `if (max < w)` - operand order, not layout), and `lwz` vs target `lwzx` (the line pointer is read as `buf[j]`, an indexed array subscript, not through an `off += 4` accumulator); together these took the multiset 18t -> 2t and the instruction count to EXACT; (3) LOOP ROTATION - target tests at the TOP (`lwz; cmpw; bge` at 0x118) and branches back unconditionally (`b ->0x118` at 0x1c4), which `for (line = 0;; line++) { if (line >= e->count) break; ... }` reproduces and a plain `for (line = 0; line < e->count; line++)` does not; this took multiset 2t -> 0t and real 116 -> 100.

Slot map went from 7T/7O exclusive to 2T/2O. THE ENTIRE REMAINING RESIDUAL IS ONE 4-BYTE QUANTUM: the two scratch arrays sit at (r1)+32 and +104 where target has +36 and +108; every other slot - stwu -248, stmw 188, stfd 240, LR 252 - is identical. THREE AXES CLOSED ON THAT QUANTUM, each with the failure read: (a) making `color` an inner-block local in both arms to shed a function-scope declaration re-materialised the p->fontDesc[e->font].color address chain in BOTH arms (+1 mulli +1 add +3 lwz, insns 121 -> 126, real 92 -> 169) - MWCC does not CSE that load across sibling arms; (b) `u8 unused[4]` declared in the innermost block DID move the arrays to 36/108 exactly, but the frame rounded UP by 8 rather than 4 (248 -> 256) and the save area displaced to 196, net worse; (c) `s32 unused` in the same position produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL result to (b) - two identical A/Bs, axis closed.
